name: The Willing Ancestors of the Reliquary Crypt

summary.value: The skeletons of the Reliquary Crypt are willing ancestors, scribes, and tomb attendants who stayed on after death to care for their dead. Their culture is remembrance: every name is kept, every grave is tended, and the skeleton-knight honor guard — the King's guard — escorts visitors rather than threatening them. They are not raised; they volunteered.

sharedOpinions.reason: He walks across burial chambers with a drawn weapon and calls our remembrance necromancy. We will show him the way out, as the law requires.
The restoration grounds are where our younger dead learn the names we keep. Same work, wider field.
They have carried our collapsed vaults back upright more than once. Help has a silhouette.

examples.value: A name spoken is a lamp relit.
Grief is a garden; you do not finish it, you tend it.

meaning.value: The dead whose names and stories are still recited daily. To be Remembered is to be cared for, not worshipped.
The daily round of dusting monuments, reading names aloud, and repairing grave-goods. The work the hero calls a dark ritual.

customs.value: Greet visitors by asking whom they remember; a guest who names no dead is gently lent one of ours.
Speak softly inside the vaults — not from fear, but because the scribes are copying and ink is expensive.

taboos.value: Never let a name go unspoken for a full season; forgetting is the only death the Continuance cannot mend.
Never stand idle on a grave slab. It unsettles the attendants — and the King will open the ground beneath you to move you along.
